_about: Launch-knob catalogue (#1465 phase 3a). DESCRIBES the launch settings a user may persist; it changes no launch behaviour. Which slugs read each knob is NOT declared here: scripts/lib/profiles/launch_knobs.py derives it from the compose text and registry-emit.sh --json exposes it per slug as `knobs`. Schema and how to add a knob: launch-knobs.md next to this file. Guard: scripts/tests/test-launch-knobs.sh.

KV_OFFLOAD_GB.description: Host-RAM KV-cache tier below the GPU pool, in GiB total across all GPUs.
KV_OFFLOAD_GB.unset: off: no host-RAM tier (the default on every compose that reads it)

source.what: entrypoint KV-offload block: `case "$$KV_OFFLOAD_GB" in *[!0-9.]*|.*|*.|*.*.*) exit 1`, i.e. digits with at most one inner dot; then --kv-offloading-size <GiB> --kv-offloading-backend native (RAM only), or a TieringOffloadingSpec with cpu_bytes_to_use = GiB * 2^30 when KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1

command KV-offload block: the same number check as vLLM, then --hicache-size int(GiB * 2^30 / 1e9 / 2) GB PER GPU and exit 1 when that is under 1 (so the total must be >= 2e9 / 2^30 = 1.8626 GiB on these 2-GPU composes); adds --enable-hierarchical-cache --mamba-max-states-per-path 1

interacts.effect: vLLM: dropped whenever the tier is on, because vLLM rejects a KV connector with expandable_segments:True

source.what: entrypoint unsets PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF inside the KV_OFFLOAD_GB branch

interacts.effect: SGLang: defaults to slru while the tier is on; an explicit value wins

source.what: adds --radix-eviction-policy slru only when RADIX_EVICTION_POLICY is empty

interacts.effect: host directory mounted at /kv-offload for the disk tier (default: <data dir>/kv-offload, i.e. ~/.local/share/club-3090/kv-offload or CLUB3090_DATA_DIR, from the launchers; the repo's gitignored kv-offload/ from a raw docker compose up)

source.what: volumes: ${KV_OFFLOAD_DIR:-${CLUB3090_DATA_DIR:-../../../../../..}/kv-offload}:/kv-offload

caveats.text: Only the dual MTP composes read it. On the vLLM DFlash tiers the same connector stores every block and never serves one back (write-only, dual-superfast measured 0 hits), so it is deliberately not wired there; SGLang DFlash2 and multi-N composes are not probed.

source.what: header rationale, and the arm that fails any other compose carrying OFFLOAD_ARGS

caveats.text: Pinned at boot: vLLM reserves the whole tier even when idle, and SGLang's host use runs above the setting (64 -> 74 GiB measured). Size it above the GPU KV pool; a smaller tier only mirrors what the GPU already holds.

source.what: HiCache trap table; the vLLM sizing note is in the vLLM compose's KV-offload comment

caveats.text: switch.sh refuses a value the host can't hold before the running slug is torn down: tier x 1.0 (vLLM) or x 74/64 (SGLang) + 28 GiB must fit in MemTotal, and on vLLM the tier must also fit in the host /dev/shm, which holds it (ipc: host; by default half of RAM, so 64 does not fit a 128 GB host). A global value applies to every reader, so on a small-RAM rig it makes every such launch refuse; a per-slug value or a shell export overrides it.

source.what: ram_error() and shm_error() (#1503), called by the resolver's check (switch.sh check_variant) and by switch.sh --set

KV_OFFLOAD_DISK.description: Adds a disk tier below the host-RAM KV tier, at /kv-offload (KV_OFFLOAD_DIR on the host).

source.what: `case "$${KV_OFFLOAD_DISK:-0}" in 0|1) ;; *) exit 1`, then exit 1 when it is 1 and KV_OFFLOAD_GB is empty; the SGLang dual MTP composes carry the same two lines

requires.why: every disk read stages through the RAM tier

source.what: "[kv-offload] KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1 needs KV_OFFLOAD_GB" then exit 1 (same on the SGLang dual MTP composes)

interacts.effect: the host directory behind /kv-offload (default <data dir>/kv-offload, on your home filesystem unless CLUB3090_DATA_DIR says otherwise); files there are written by root in the container

source.what: volumes line and the KV_OFFLOAD_DISK comment in the entrypoint

interacts.effect: SGLang only: optional cap; there is no cap otherwise

source.what: SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_MAX_SIZE is exported only when KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB is set

caveats.text: Uncapped by default, by maintainer decision (discussion #1419): never invent a default cap. vLLM's fs tier grows until the disk is full; SGLang's is capped only by KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB and always keeps 20 GiB free.

source.what: "the fs tier has NO size cap - it grows until the disk is full"; the SGLang compose exports SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_MIN_FREE_SPACE=20Gi

caveats.text: SGLang writes about one file per token per GPU (a 40K session is ~89K files) and switches storage prefetch to wait_complete, because the default timeout silently re-prefilled every disk hit on a large directory.

source.what: Disk tier paragraph (2026-09-25 measurements)

KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB.description: Caps SGLang's disk KV tier, in whole GiB total across both GPUs.
KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB.unset: no cap (the disk tier grows until only 20 GiB of the volume is free)

source.what: `case "$$KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB" in *[!0-9]*|0) exit 1`; exit 1 unless KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1; SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_MAX_SIZE = GiB * 1024 / 2 Mi per GPU

requires.why: it caps the disk tier, which is off unless KV_OFFLOAD_DISK=1

source.what: "KV_OFFLOAD_DISK_GB is set but KV_OFFLOAD_DISK is not 1" then exit 1

caveats.text: vLLM has no equivalent: its fs tier cannot be capped, so no vLLM compose reads this knob.

source.what: KV_OFFLOAD_DISK comment: the fs tier has NO size cap

caveats.text: Split evenly per GPU and enforced per model directory; measured 1.43 GiB per GPU under a 1.5 GiB-per-GPU cap after 3 sessions, LRU eviction.

ENABLE_THINKING.description: Server-default thinking mode for requests that don't set their own.
ENABLE_THINKING.unset: the compose default: true on the Qwen3.8 family and Nemotron, false on vllm/thinkingcap-dual-w4a8

source.what: --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": ${ENABLE_THINKING:-true}, ...}': the value is spliced into the JSON as a bare literal, so only true|false make valid JSON (issue #1465 gotcha 6: `on` stops vLLM from starting); the entrypoint picks the thinking sampler row only on the exact string true
--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": ${ENABLE_THINKING:-false}}' (JSON splice, default off)

_think="${ENABLE_THINKING:-true}" is spliced bare into the JSON of --default-chat-template-kwargs, so a non-JSON value makes that argument invalid JSON (how SGLang then reacts is not measured here); the sampler row is the thinking one only on the exact string true

interacts.effect: Qwen3.8 family (vLLM and SGLang): false makes the effort default inert, because the chat template reads reasoning_effort only when thinking is on

source.what: the effort branch sits inside {%- if enable_thinking is undefined or enable_thinking is true %}

interacts.effect: Qwen3.8 family: selects the model-card sampler row (thinking 1.0/0.95/0.0 vs instruct 0.7/0.80/1.5 for temp/top_p/presence); an explicit TEMP, TOP_P or PRESENCE_PENALTY still wins

source.what: "Sampler follows the reasoning mode" block in the entrypoint

caveats.text: SGLang with false: thinking goes off but the engine keeps serving the thinking sampler row from generation_config.json; clients must send temperature/top_p/presence_penalty to get the instruct row.

source.what: the [sampler] warning printed on the instruct branch

caveats.text: The per-model thinking pin (CLUB3090_THINKING_<MODEL> = on|off) is a resolver layer between the slug's own value and the global one: on -> true, off -> false. It reaches only the slugs of that model whose compose reads ENABLE_THINKING; on the others (the llama.cpp Qwen3.8 composes use REASONING=on|off instead) switch.sh warns that it has no effect.

source.what: PIN_VALUES and the `model pin` layer in resolve()

REASONING_EFFORT.description: Server-default reasoning effort for requests that don't send their own.
REASONING_EFFORT.unset: the compose default: low (Qwen3.8 vLLM/SGLang, Inkling-Small), medium (Qwen3.8 llama.cpp), max (GLM-5.3-Flash)

source.what: spliced unvalidated into --default-chat-template-kwargs as "reasoning_effort": "${REASONING_EFFORT:-low}"; the mounted patched template maps high/max -> xhigh and minimal -> low and raises on anything else at render, so a bad default boots fine and then fails every request that sends no effort of its own (HTTP 400)

`case "$$_reff" in low|medium|xhigh) : ;; *) exit 1`; passed as default_reasoning_effort, not reasoning_effort, because SGLang <= 0.5.20 lets a default reasoning_effort override the request's (sglang#38104). Stricter than vLLM: high/minimal/max are refused at boot although the same template would map them

LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS=${LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS:-{"reasoning_effort":"${REASONING_EFFORT:-medium}"}}, unvalidated; per the compose header the GGUF's embedded template silently turns high into xhigh (the slowest level). Whether it raises on other values is not recorded in the repo
--reasoning-effort '${REASONING_EFFORT:-max}', unvalidated; the comment above it lists the family's values as max (vendor default) | high | low and records that `none` is silently ignored
--chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"${REASONING_EFFORT:-low}"}', unvalidated; the header lists none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max and the model ignores enable_thinking entirely

interacts.effect: Qwen3.8 family on vLLM and SGLang: inert when ENABLE_THINKING=false

source.what: the effort branch is inside the enable_thinking check

interacts.effect: llama.cpp Qwen3.8: REASONING_EFFORT is only the default of this variable, so setting LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS makes it ignored

source.what: LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS=${LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS:-{...${REASONING_EFFORT:-medium}...}}

caveats.text: Only the fallback for clients that send no effort: a request's own reasoning_effort wins on every engine here.

source.what: "It is a PER-REQUEST OpenAI control, so this is only the fallback for callers that send nothing"

caveats.text: The levels are not a scale on Qwen3.8: low injects a brevity instruction, medium injects nothing (the un-nudged baseline), xhigh injects a careful-thinking one. The instruction sits at the top of the system prompt, so changing the default changes every prompt's prefix and the prefix cache starts over.

source.what: reasoning_instructions for xhigh/low, rendered first in the system block

caveats.text: On GLM-5.3-Flash it is effectively a two-position switch: low = thinking off (0 reasoning chars measured), max = on; high measured next to low, not between.

source.what: measurements in the thinking/reasoning policy comment

caveats.text: Inkling-Small also documents a float 0.0-0.99; it is left out of the domain because the compose splices the value into a JSON string ("0.5"), and whether the template accepts that string form is not recorded.

source.what: header: reads reasoning_effort (none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max, or a float 0.0-0.99)

SPEC_N.description: Speculative-decoding depth for the slug's drafter; 0 turns the drafter off.
SPEC_N.unset: the compose's own depth (per slug; 1 to 8 today, or inferred from the drafter on the SGLang DFlash2 composes)

source.what: `case "$$_spec_n" in ""|*[!0-9]*) exit 1` ("a typo can never masquerade as a silent drafter off"); every compose that reads SPEC_N carries the same *[!0-9]* check and a 0 = off branch

interacts.effect: SPEC=off|OFF|Off|false|no|0 forces the drafter off whatever SPEC_N says (back-compat alias)

source.what: case "$${SPEC:-}" in off|OFF|Off|false|no|0) _spec_n=0

interacts.effect: SGLang MTP composes: SPEC_N=0 lowers the default mem-fraction-static from 0.95 to 0.90 (room for CUDA graphs without the drafter)

source.what: the SPEC_N=0 branch exports MEM_FRACTION=0.90 when it is unset

interacts.effect: older per-compose depth names (MTP_DRAFT_N_MAX, DRAFT_N_MAX, MTP_N_MAX, SPEC_N_MAX, NUM_SPEC_TOKENS) are the fallback when SPEC_N is unset on some llama.cpp, beellama and vLLM composes

source.what: _spec_n="$${SPEC_N:-$${MTP_DRAFT_N_MAX:-2}}" (and siblings)

caveats.text: The number means different things per slug: MTP depth, DFlash/DFlash2 draft width or block size, the ngram-mod length, or exllamav3's draft ceiling. Defaults are tuned per slug, so a global value other than 0 overrides every slug's tuning at once.

source.what: "SPEC_N=<n> sets the draft ceiling"; the other meanings are in the vLLM DFlash2, SGLang DFlash2 and qwen3.8-flash-next llama.cpp composes

caveats.text: Measured on vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-max: with the MTP drafter on, prefix reuse snaps to the attention-block boundary (zero below about two blocks, ~3.2K tokens there); with SPEC_N=0 it reuses at 16-token granularity. Turning the drafter off trades decode speed for that.
